title: Atoms and Molecules
seo_title: Secondary 1 Science: Atoms and Molecules Worksheets (Lower Secondary Science with Answers)
standard_code: Secondary 1: Model of Matter – Atoms and Molecules
standard_text: Describe an atom as electrically neutral, with a positively charged nucleus of protons and neutrons and negatively charged electrons moving around it; recognise that the mass of an atom is mainly in its nucleus and that atoms of an element have a unique number of protons; describe a molecule as two or more atoms chemically combined and state the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 science worksheets for Singapore students on atoms and molecules: protons, neutrons and electrons, proton and nucleon numbers, molecules and chemical formulae. With answers.
key_big: Protons (+) and neutrons in the nucleus; electrons (−) around it.
body_html:
How to think about it

An atom has a tiny positive nucleus (protons and neutrons) with negative electrons moving around it.

  • Proton: +. Neutron: no charge. Electron: −. Atoms are neutral: protons = electrons.
  • Proton number = number of protons; it identifies the element. Neutrons = nucleon number − proton number.
  • A molecule is two or more atoms chemically combined: O₂ (element), H₂O (compound).
  • In a formula, the small number after a symbol is the number of those atoms: CO₂ has 1 C and 2 O.
Example

Sodium: proton number 11, nucleon number 23. Neutrons?

23 − 11

Answer: 12

Example

How many atoms are in one molecule of NH₃?

1 N + 3 H

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

  • Saying neutrons are negative. They have no charge.
  • Putting electrons in the nucleus. They move around it.
  • Thinking the neutron number identifies the element. It is the proton number.
  • Counting CO₂ as 2 atoms. It has 3: 1 carbon and 2 oxygen.

faq.a: It has the same number of protons (positive) and electrons (negative).

faq.q: How do you find the number of neutrons?
faq.a: Subtract the proton number from the nucleon number.

items.q: Which particle in an atom has no charge and is in the nucleus?
items.e: Protons (+) and neutrons (0) are in the nucleus; electrons (−) move around it.

items.q: An atom of fluorine (F) has a proton number of 9 and a nucleon number of 19. How many protons does it have?
items.e: The proton number is the number of protons.

items.q: Where is an electron found in an atom?

items.q: Where is most of the mass of an atom?
items.e: Protons and neutrons are much heavier than electrons.

items.q: An atom has 6 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: Every atom of carbon has 6 protons; the proton number identifies the element.

items.q: Which particle in an atom has negative (−) and is moving around the nucleus?
items.e: Protons (+) and neutrons (0) are in the nucleus; electrons (−) move around it.

items.q: What makes atoms of one element different from atoms of another element?

items.q: Why do scientists change models of the atom over time?
c: New evidence from experiments shows that the old model needs improving.
Atoms change their structure each year.
items.e: Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr each improved the model.

items.q: What is the charge on a neutron?

items.q: Why is an atom electrically neutral?
c: It has no particles with charge.
Its electrons are in the nucleus.
It has more neutrons than protons.
It has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
items.e: The positive and negative charges cancel.
